title: Comprehensive Security & Compliance Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Avery Chen
content:
Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational procedures for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC, incident response (security), compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is intended for engineering leads, security reviewers, product owners, and compliance auditors.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-managed environments (hosted, dedicated, private) and control plane components.
- Excludes third-party managed customer data stores where the customer explicitly manages retention (see Data Residency section for exceptions).

Owner & Review Cadence
- Primary owner: Security Team (owner: Avery Chen)
- Secondary owners: Eng-Infra (logging and retention plumbing), Eng-SRE (SLOs and alerts), Product (data residency contracts)
- Review cadence: quarterly for operational controls, annual for policy-level changes; RBAC reviews every 90 days.

1) RBAC & Authentication
Overview
- All human and machine identities must be managed via the central Identity system (Okta for human identities with SCIM provisioning; identity-service for internal service accounts).
- Principle of least privilege enforced by role-based access control (RBAC) and automated policy checks during PRs and provisioning.

Role Naming & Scoping Conventions
- Roles: team-{team-name}-{env}-{level} (examples: team-serving-runtime-prod-admin, team-sre-staging-readonly).
- Avoid org-wide wildcards; use resource-level scoping where supported.

Access Lifecycle (onboard/offboard/change)
1. Access requested via Access Portal (cloud: https://access.redwood.internal) with justification and business owner approval.
2. Automated SCIM assignment for Okta groups; service accounts created via identity-service with short-lived credentials (default TTL 12 hours).
3. All access changes trigger an approver review and generate an Audit Event (see Audit Logging).
4. Offboard checklist: disable Okta account, remove SCIM group membership, rotate/seal any associated secrets in Vault, and document completion in ticket.

MFA, SSO & Authentication Controls
- All human users: SSO via Okta + MFA (TOTP + device-based risk evaluation).
- Service-to-service auth: mTLS where possible; otherwise short-lived JWTs issued by identity-service using KS (Key Service) signed keys.
- Emergency (break-glass) access: limited to senior SREs and Security on-call; requires JIT approval flow and automatic session recording. Break-glass expiry: 8 hours.

Periodic Reviews & Enforcement
- RBAC reviews: every 90 days; tool: rbac-reviewer (cron job) enumerates group membership and flags stale accounts (>60 days inactive).
- Policy-as-Code: access policies enforced by terraform-iam-checker in CI; PRs that widen access fail gating.
- SLO: auth-service availability >= 99.99% monthly; incident threshold: 5m outage triggers P1 process.

2) Audit Logging
Goal
- Produce a complete, tamper-evident audit trail for identity, access, config changes, data access, and security incidents.

Event Types & Minimum Schema
- Required event categories: authentication, authorization decision, role/group change, secret/credential rotation, storage access (read/write/delete), config/deployment change, incident actions.
- Log schema (JSON): timestamp, event_id, service, event_type, actor_id, actor_type, target_resource, action, result, request_id, ip, region, meta (string).

Retention & Storage
- System audit logs (auth, role changes, config changes): 7 years, stored immutably under s3://redwood-compliance/audit/immutable/YYYY/ with object-lock configured.
- Access logs (application-level read/write): 365 days by default; for regulated customers retention may be extended per contract up to 7 years.
- SIEM forwarding: real-time forward to Splunk and Datadog; ingestion SLO for critical events: <30s.

Integrity & Tamper Evidence
- All audit bundles signed and hashed; daily manifests are published to internal artifact-store and checksummed to support chain-of-custody.
- Immutable backups: nightly snapshot stored in a separate account with MFA-delete enabled.

Log Access & Queries
- Access to raw audit data is restricted: only Security, SRE, and designated Compliance roles. Queries should be executed via the Audit Query UI to prevent exfiltration of raw data.
- Example query (Splunk):
  index=audit event_type="role_change" | stats count by actor_id, target_resource

3) Data Residency & Retention
Residency Controls
- Customers can select region(s) for PII and customer content. For private deployments, customer-managed storage is preferred. For hosted mode, customer data is stored in the selected cloud region (AWS: us-west-2, eu-west-1, etc.).
- Default residency: US and EU regions only; APAC upon contract.

Retention Policy (default tiers)
- Ephemeral request logs: 30 days (internal cache + aggregated metrics retained per Optimize policies).
- Application/usage logs (non-PII): 365 days.
- Auth & security audit events: 7 years.
- Customer content (per contract): configurable; default 365 days unless otherwise specified in SLA.

Data Deletion & Proof of Deletion
- Deletion requests follow the Data Deletion Procedure: submit request -> verify identity -> schedule deletion job -> create deletion proof (signed manifest + S3 delete markers) -> record in evidence repo.
- Proof format: signed JSON manifest with object checksums, deletion timestamps, and operator_id. Example proof schema (JSON snippet):
  {"deletion_job_id":"dj-20251201-01","owner":"customer-123","deleted_paths":["s3://customer-123/content/2025-..."],"deleted_at":"2025-12-01T04:05:06Z","signature":"..."}

4) Secure SDLC
Policy Overview
- Security gates are enforced at multiple stages: design review, code review, CI pipelines, and release. All public-facing and model-serving changes require a Security Design Review (SDR) for threat modelling.

Required Checks & Tooling
- Static Analysis: Snyk/Dependabot alerts integrated into GitHub; high/critical vulnerabilities require PR hold and triage within 48 hours.
- Secrets Detection: pre-commit hooks and CI scan; any detected secret fail the build. Rotate leaked credentials immediately via Vault.
- IaC Scanning: terraform-iam-checker and tflint; policy violations block merge.
- Dependency / Licenses: automated license checks; non-compliant licenses escalate to Legal.

Release Controls
- Production releases: must pass canary rollout (10% for 30 minutes with rollback criteria), automated QA checks, and chaos-testing for core runtime services every release cycle.
- Rollout policy recorded in Release PR includes: owner, rollback plan, backoff thresholds, and traffic weight schedule.

Developer Onboarding & Security Training
- Mandatory secure-coding course for engineers; refresher every 12 months.

5) Incident Response (Security) Procedures
TL;DR
- Follow standard IR runbook for security incidents. Key difference: for incidents affecting customer data or residency, notify affected customers per SLA and engage Legal and Customer Success immediately.

Incident Classification & SLOs
- Severity levels: P1 (data exfiltration / production-wide outage), P2 (service degradation with potential security exposure), P3 (limited impact), P4 (informational).
- Notification SLOs: P1 notify within 1 hour, P2 within 4 hours. Public status update cadence: hourly for P1 until mitigation.

Initial Triage Steps (first 60 minutes)
1. Triage: SRE + Security on-call acknowledge alert and create incident channel (#inc-<id>).
2. Containment: isolate affected services, rotate relevant credentials, and enable additional logging.
3. Evidence Preservation: snapshot impacted hosts, export audit logs, and preserve network captures in secure evidence bucket (s3://redwood-compliance/incidents/<incident-id>/).

Forensics & Root Cause
- Use dedicated forensics image and immutable storage for artifacts. For complex incidents, engage external forensics vendor (pre-approved contract: VendorSec Forensics).

Customer Notification & Regulatory Reporting
- Data breach determination: if confirmed, follow notification timelines in customer contracts and applicable law (e.g., GDPR 72-hour window). Legal and Customer Success coordinate notifications.

Post-Incident
- Postmortem published within 7 days for P1/P2 incidents, including timeline, mitigations, action items, and owners. Remediations tracked to closure and validated via tests.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Purpose
- Provide auditable packages that map controls to artifacts for ISO/ SOC / GDPR or customer SOC2/PCI requests.

Evidence Cataloging
- Evidence artifacts stored under s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/<standard>/<year>/<control-id>/ with metadata index in the Evidence Registry (internal service).
- Typical artifacts: architecture diagrams, access control snapshots (RBAC export), audit log manifests, change tickets, test results, policy documents, training records, and encryption key rotation logs.

Evidence Request Process
1. Request submitted via Evidence Portal -> Evidence Owner assigned.
2. Evidence owner assembles artifacts, validates signatures/checksums, and packages with control-mapping spreadsheet.
3. Package delivered to auditor via secure share (short-lived URL, access logged).

Example Control Mapping Table (plaintext):
- CONTROL: Access control review -> ARTIFACT: RBAC export (2025-11-01), OWNER: Security, PATH: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/ISO27001/2025/AC-2/rbac-export-20251101.json

7) Risk & Exceptions
Exception Request Criteria
- Exceptions are intended for temporary gaps where compensating controls can mitigate risk. Permanent exceptions require executive-level review and legal sign-off.

Approval Workflow
1. Owner files exception request with risk assessment and compensating controls.
2. Security reviews and assigns risk rating (Low/Medium/High).
3. For Medium or High risks, Compliance and CTO sign-off required. High risks may require mitigation plan with milestones.
4. Exceptions auto-expire (max 90 days) unless renewed with justification and new approvals.

Required Exception Fields (example JSON snippet):
{"request_id":"ex-20251215-001","owner":"team-serving-runtime","control":"AC-2","justification":"Feature requires temporary write access for migration","compensating_controls":"Enhanced logging + IP restriction","risk_rating":"Medium","expires_at":"2026-03-15"}

Compensating Controls Examples
- Network-level microsegmentation, additional monitoring via IDS, mandatory weekly access attestation, temporary read-only views for non-prod.

- Evidence Portal: https://evidence.redwood.internal
- Access Portal: https://access.redwood.internal
- Identity provider: Okta (SCIM), identity-service (internal)
- Audit pipeline: audit-logger -> kafka-logs -> splunk-forwarder
- Evidence store: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/
